physics.forces-motion-describe-kb.0014.a: gradient = change in distance / change in time = speed; steeper = faster (choose two points, divide rise by run)
physics.forces-motion-describe-kb.0014.b: area under velocity-time graph = distance travelled; calculate area (e.g. triangles/rectangles)

physics.forces-motion-recall-kb.0012.b: velocity has direction (vector), speed does not (scalar)

physics.hl-graph.0004.a: read time for count rate to halve from graph (e.g. 600 to 300); cannot read exact value from labels only
physics.hl-graph.0004.b: use half-lives elapsed in 60 days; value depends on (a)

physics.magnetism-em-describe-kb.0011.a: wrap insulated wire coil around soft iron core (nail), connect to d.c. supply/cell, switch on; test by picking up paperclips
physics.magnetism-em-describe-kb.0011.b: wire vertically through horizontal card; place compasses around wire; switch on current; mark direction of needles; join to show concentric circles

physics.magnetism-em-explain-kb.0012.a: current produces magnetic field around wire; interacts with permanent magnet field giving force (motor effect)
physics.magnetism-em-explain-kb.0012.b: electromagnet can be switched off to release scrap; strength can be varied/very strong
physics.magnetism-em-explain-kb.0012.c: a.c. current reverses direction at supply frequency; force on coil in magnetic field reverses each time so cone moves back and forth at same frequency

physics.magnetism-em-extended-kb.0008.a: more turns; larger current (or soft iron core)
physics.magnetism-em-extended-kb.0008.b: current in coil in magnetic field; force on each side (motor effect) in opposite directions -> turning effect; split-ring commutator reverses current every half turn so continues rotating; brushes contact. Speed up: more current, stronger magnet, more turns. Reverse direction: reverse current or reverse magnet poles

physics.magnetism-em-recall-kb.0012.a: increase current; stronger magnetic field (or longer wire in field)
physics.magnetism-em-recall-kb.0012.c: beam deflected in a circular path (force perpendicular to motion)

physics.magnetism-induction-describe-kb..a: needle deflects one way as magnet enters, then opposite way (larger, as faster) as it leaves; zero in middle
physics.magnetism-induction-describe-kb..b: kinetic energy of wind -> kinetic energy of blades/rotor -> electrical energy (some wasted as heat/sound)

physics.magnetism-induction-explain-kb.0.a: current flows in coil; current-carrying coil in magnetic field experiences force opposing motion (Lenz), so more work needed
physics.magnetism-induction-explain-kb.0.b: faster rate of cutting field lines / change of flux -> larger induced voltage/current

physics.magnetism-induction-extended-kb..a: move magnet faster; stronger magnet; more turns on coil
physics.magnetism-induction-extended-kb..b: connect coil to sensitive ammeter/galvanometer; push magnet in -> deflection; hold still -> zero; pull out -> opposite deflection. Size: speed, magnet strength, turns, coil area. Direction: direction of motion, which pole

physics.magnetism-induction-mcq-kb.0008.a: induces a current in the opposite direction

physics.magnetism-induction-recall-kb.00.all: reverse direction of motion of magnet; reverse the poles (turn magnet round)

physics.magnetism-magnets-describe-kb.00.a: field lines from N to S pole, curving around magnet; lines closest/strongest at poles; lines never cross
physics.magnetism-magnets-describe-kb.00.b: paperclip becomes induced magnet (attracted); steel retains magnetism when removed (permanent magnet, hard material)

physics.magnetism-magnets-recall-kb.0013.a: hard material retains magnetism (hard to magnetise/demagnetise, e.g. steel); soft loses it easily (e.g. iron)

physics.magnetism-transformers-explain-k.a: a.c. in primary produces changing magnetic field; iron core carries it to secondary; changing field induces alternating voltage in secondary
physics.magnetism-transformers-explain-k.b: for same power P=IV, high V means low current; power loss I²R in cables smaller so less heating
physics.magnetism-transformers-explain-k.c: high voltages dangerous in homes; reduce to safe 230 V for appliances

physics.magnetism-transformers-mcq-kb.00.a: more turns on the secondary coil than the primary

physics.magnetism-transformers-recall-kb.b: between transmission lines and homes/consumers (local substations)

physics.matter-density-explain-kb.0009.a: sharp knife smaller area; same force gives greater pressure
physics.matter-density-explain-kb.0009.b: pressure increases with depth (p = ρgh); greater force at bottom
physics.matter-density-explain-kb.0009.c: wood less dense than water; iron denser than water

physics.matter-gases-explain-kb.0005.all: gas molecules gain kinetic energy, move faster; hit walls harder/more often, pressure rises inside so balloon expands

physics.matter-gases-mcq-kb.0003.all: molecules colliding with the container walls

physics.matter-gases-recall-kb.0012.c: random motion, high speeds, in all directions, colliding with each other and walls

physics.matter-state-describe-kb.0007.a: solid: vibrate about fixed positions; liquid: move around/slide past each other; gas: move randomly at high speed, far apart
physics.matter-state-describe-kb.0007.b: particles gain energy, vibrate more, break free of fixed positions, can move past each other
physics.matter-state-describe-kb.0007.c: particles lose energy, slow down, move closer together, form liquid (attractive forces hold them)

physics.matter-state-explain-kb.0007.a: sweat evaporates; most energetic molecules escape, taking energy from skin so it cools
physics.matter-state-explain-kb.0007.b: gas particles far apart with space between; solid particles tightly packed touching
